title: Grade 8 Science — Mon, May 25
description: Microorganisms — Day 1 of 5: What are microorganisms? Types and where they live
subject: science

questions.question: Microorganisms are:
options: Large organisms visible to the naked eye
Living organisms so small they can only be seen under a microscope
questions.explanation: Microorganisms (microbes) are living organisms too small to be seen without a microscope. 'Micro' = tiny. Examples: bacteria, virus, fungi, protozoa, algae.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to study microorganisms?
questions.explanation: A microscope magnifies objects too small to see with the naked eye. Light microscope (×1000 magnification) can see bacteria; electron microscope (×1,000,000) can see viruses.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major group of microorganisms?
questions.explanation: The 5 main groups of microorganisms: Bacteria, Virus (some scientists don't classify as 'living'), Fungi, Protozoa, Algae. Insects are visible to naked eye and are NOT microorganisms.

questions.question: Bacteria are:
questions.explanation: Bacteria = unicellular (single-celled), prokaryotic (no membrane-bound nucleus). They are the most abundant organisms on Earth. Found everywhere: soil, water, air, inside our bodies.

questions.question: Viruses are different from bacteria because viruses:
options: Can survive without a host cell and make their own food
Cannot reproduce on their own — they need a living host cell
Are visible to the naked eye
questions.explanation: Viruses are NOT cells. They are just genetic material (DNA/RNA) wrapped in protein. They MUST enter a living host cell to replicate. They are not considered truly 'living' by many scientists.

questions.question: Fungi include:
questions.explanation: Fungi include: mushrooms (large, visible), yeast (unicellular, microscopic), mould/mildew (multicellular, microscopic). Bread mould = Rhizopus. Yeast = Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

questions.question: Protozoa are:
questions.explanation: Protozoa = unicellular, animal-like. Examples: Amoeba (moves with pseudopodia), Paramecium (uses cilia), Plasmodium (causes malaria). Many are parasites.

questions.question: Algae are unique microorganisms because they:
options: Are plant-like and can photosynthesise to make their own food
questions.explanation: Algae contain chlorophyll and can photosynthesise. Examples: Spirogyra (freshwater, thread-like), Chlamydomonas (unicellular). Marine algae produce ~50% of Earth's oxygen!

questions.question: Where can microorganisms be found?
options: Everywhere — in air, water, soil, inside living things, in extreme environments
questions.explanation: Microorganisms are found EVERYWHERE: in Arctic ice, hot springs, deep ocean, soil, air, inside our bodies, on our skin. They are the most versatile life forms on Earth.

questions.question: Microorganisms that need oxygen to survive are called:
questions.explanation: Aerobes = need oxygen (aerobic respiration). Anaerobes = survive WITHOUT oxygen. Example: Clostridium (causes tetanus) is anaerobic. Rhizobium (nitrogen fixation) is aerobic.

questions.question: The scientist who first observed microorganisms under a microscope was:
questions.explanation: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1670s) first observed microorganisms ('animalcules') using his hand-crafted microscopes. Louis Pasteur proved germ theory. Robert Koch identified TB and cholera bacteria.

questions.question: Which microorganism causes malaria?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium (a protozoan parasite), transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. The mosquito is the vector — it transmits but doesn't cause the disease.

questions.question: Algae vs bacteria vs virus: which ONE is photosynthetic?
questions.explanation: Algae contain chlorophyll and photosynthesise. Some bacteria (cyanobacteria) also photosynthesise. Viruses cannot photosynthesise — they aren't even cells. Algae is the most clearly photosynthetic group.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct size order from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: Size: Virus (20–300 nm) < Bacteria (1–10 μm) < Protozoa (10–100+ μm). Viruses are 10–100× smaller than bacteria. You need an electron microscope to see viruses.

questions.question: Summary: the 5 main groups of microorganisms are:
questions.explanation: The 5 major groups: BACTERIA (prokaryote), VIRUS (non-cellular), FUNGI (yeast/mould/mushroom), PROTOZOA (animal-like unicellular), ALGAE (plant-like, photosynthetic). Each has distinct characteristics.
